story.headline: Wawrinka's last tournament starts in Basel
story.summary: Stan Wawrinka, 41, plays his last career tournament at the Swiss Indoors in Basel, opening against Jiri Lehecka on Tuesday 27 October.
story.display_body: Stan Wawrinka, 41, three-time Grand Slam champion and a former world No. 3, ends a 25-year career at his home-country tournament. The draw gave him the hardest opener available: Jiri Lehecka of the Czech Republic (ATP 20), who reached the Miami Masters final and the Tokyo final this year, losing the latter to Carlos Alcaraz. They have never met. Wawrinka is ranked 140th and will play what SRF counts as his 985th singles match on tour; a tribute ceremony is planned for Monday 26 October, the evening before. Novak Djokovic, 39, returns to Basel after 15 years on a wildcard (a tournament-granted entry) fresh from winning Beijing, and the other Swiss wildcards face tough draws too: Jérôme Kym against Arthur Rinderknech (ATP 61), Dominic Stricker against Casper Ruud (ATP 24). The tournament's own site confirms Rémy Bertola and Mika Brunold came through qualifying into the main draw
story.why: a 41-year-old ranked 140th faces a top-20 opponent in his final match, so Tuesday could be a short farewell; the ceremony on Monday is the guaranteed part.

story.headline: Antonelli wins Austin, title waits
story.summary: Kimi Antonelli won the US Grand Prix but Russell and Hamilton scored just enough to keep the title mathematically open until Mexico.
story.display_body: Kimi Antonelli, 20, won from pole by 13 seconds for his ninth victory of the season, with Charles Leclerc second and Max Verstappen third. He could not be crowned because Mercedes team-mate George Russell (eighth) and Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari, fourth) scored just enough to stay mathematically alive: Antonelli has 365 points, 123 ahead of Russell and 124 ahead of Hamilton, with five rounds and 125 points left. Verstappen, Leclerc and Lando Norris (fifth) are now out of title contention (Autosport, 25 Oct). He can clinch at next weekend's Mexico Grand Prix; Autosport's calculation says that because he leads in wins, Russell would need to win and Antonelli finish no higher than tenth, with Hamilton needing the same. At Baku four weeks ago his lead was 66 points. Audi scored nothing (Hülkenberg 11th, Bortoleto 13th). Autosport notes the Qatar and Abu Dhabi races are assumed to go ahead "amid the conflict".
story.why: barring a collapse, F1 gets its youngest world champion in Mexico.

story.headline: Lugano lead; Basel stall at 0-0
story.summary: Lugano beat Thun to lead the Super League while Basel, held 0-0 by GC, are seventh.
story.display_body: Lugano, who also won at Thun on Sunday, top the 12-team table on 31 points from 11 games (ten wins, one draw), six clear of Young Boys on 25 (BBC table, updated 25 Oct) (table). Basel, drew 0-0 at home with Grasshoppers after three straight defeats (SRF); they sit seventh on 14 points — currently in the bottom-half "relegation round" slot, a split that happens after 33 games and sets who plays for the title. Basel travel to leaders Lugano next Sunday, 1 November. Sion beat Lausanne narrowly on Sunday; Lausanne are bottom.
story.why: six points with 22 games left is not decisive, but Lugano are unbeaten and Basel have not won in their last three league games.

story.headline: Swiss FA admits Fernandes red card was wrong
story.summary: The SFV says Edimilson Fernandes should only have been booked in YB's 2-0 win over St. Gallen.
story.display_body: The Swiss Football Association's refereeing department says a yellow card, not a red, was the correct call for Edimilson Fernandes' challenge in Young Boys' 2-0 win over St. Gallen, even though referee Lukas Fähndrich reviewed it on video after VAR (video assistant referee) intervened. Even the fouled St. Gallen player, Görtler, called a yellow acceptable. What happens to the ban is open: under the Swiss Football League's precedent a second direct red this season means four matches, as for Thun's Marco Bürki, though Sion's Fodé Sylla got only two. [Single-source: SRF reporting the SFV's wording.]
story.why: an admitted error does not automatically undo a suspension, and with YB second the length of Fernandes' ban will decide how much it hurts.

story.headline: Real win the Clasico at Camp Nou
story.summary: Real Madrid beat Barcelona 2-1 at Camp Nou, cutting the La Liga gap to three points.
story.display_body: Kylian Mbappé scored twice, the second a late winner, in a 2-1 Real Madrid win at the Camp Nou (Barcelona's home ground). The result ended Barcelona's nine-game unbeaten domestic run and cut their league lead from a potential nine points to three. Jose Mourinho, back in charge of Real Madrid, is now six Clásicos unbeaten (four wins, two draws) in his second spell; Barcelona coach Hansi Flick said his side "lacked freshness". [Single-source: BBC; the official La Liga page was not reached.]
story.why: the title race in Spain is live again, with Real five wins in a row in all competitions.

story.headline: Carrick close to exit after Bournemouth loss
story.summary: Man Utd lost 3-0 at home to Bournemouth, an eighth game without a win.
story.display_body: United are winless in eight matches in all competitions, the club's worst run since 2015-16, after the home defeat following a 4-1 loss at Como in the same week. Manager Michael Carrick, who would not say whether he will take the trip to Chelsea next Saturday, 31 October, said "the responsibility is mine". BBC's United reporter says the club's owners are in "serious talks" about his future — and that fans' booing at the players, not him, suggests that replacing the manager will not fix what supporters see as deeper problems. [Single-source: BBC; reports of replacement candidates are gossip and not reported here.]
story.why: a dismissal would be United's third managerial change in three seasons.

story.headline: Marquez leads after Martin's crash
story.summary: Jorge Martin broke his forearm in the Phillip Island sprint and the Australian GP was cancelled, leaving Marquez ahead.
story.display_body: Marc Marquez (Ducati) won Saturday's sprint (a short half-distance race) as his title rival Jorge Martin crashed out of second, which gave Marquez a 10-point championship lead (Autosport, 24 Oct). Aprilia said Martin fractured his forearm radius with a suspected ulna fracture and was ruled out of Sunday (Autosport, 24 Oct). The Sunday race, the last ever at Phillip Island on the schedule, was then cancelled because low visibility grounded the medical helicopter MotoGP rules require; riders did a farewell lap behind a safety car. Autosport's reports did not say how points would be handled for the cancelled race.
story.why: Martin's injury hands Marquez a clear edge with the Qatar round (riders have asked for safety guarantees) still to come, though the remaining calendar was not confirmed in these reports.

story.headline: Josi three assists as Swiss NHLers shine
story.summary: Roman Josi had three assists, Lian Bichsel his first point of the season and Akira Schmid won in goal.
story.display_body: Roman Josi, captain of the Nashville Predators, had three assists in a 6-2 win over Colorado, his first three-point game since last February; he has 11 assists in 11 games, eighth in the league. Dallas's Lian Bichsel, 22, got his first point of the season in a 6-3 win over the Islanders with a plus-4 rating, and Florida's Akira Schmid made 19 saves in a 3-2 win at Chicago.
story.why: a quiet but notable night for the Swiss contingent in the NHL.

story.headline: Lula wins fourth term, Bolsonaro cries foul
story.summary: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Brazil's presidential runoff on Sunday 25 October with 51.79% of the vote to 48.21% for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, and Bolsonaro refused to concede, saying he would ask for the election to be annulled.
story.display_body: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Brazil's presidential runoff on Sunday 25 October with 51.79% of the vote to 48.21% for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, and Bolsonaro refused to concede, saying he would ask for the election to be annulled. The result reverses the first round of Sunday 4 October, when Bolsonaro led 47% to 45%; RFI's São Paulo correspondent says no candidate who finished second in a Brazilian first round had ever gone on to win. Abstention and blank or spoiled ballots were the lowest in 20 years. Bolsonaro's challenge rests on a two-hour extension of polling hours, which a Supreme Court judge ordered after public-transport problems were reported, at the request of Lula's campaign. Bolsonaro's own campaign had asked for extensions in some southern states hit by flooding, and the president of the electoral court, Kassio Nunes Marques, said the extension did not influence the vote. Legal experts quoted by DW doubt the complaint meets the threshold for annulment. In his victory speech Lula, who turns 81 on Tuesday 27 October, said voters had defeated the "interference" of digital platforms and promised to regulate them. He will face the most conservative Congress since Brazil's return to democracy in the 1980s: Bolsonaro's Liberal Party and its allies could hold more than 280 of 513 lower-house seats.
story.why: Latin America's largest country stays with a left-wing government that has clashed with Washington over trade, but a hostile Congress and a contested result may limit what Lula can do in his fourth term.

story.headline: Vučić concedes Serbia to student movement
story.summary: Aleksandar Vučić conceded defeat in Serbia's snap parliamentary election on the evening of Sunday 25 October, after projections gave the student-led Students' List a majority in the 250-seat parliament.
story.display_body: Aleksandar Vučić conceded defeat in Serbia's snap parliamentary election on the evening of Sunday 25 October, after projections gave the student-led Students' List a majority in the 250-seat parliament. "Based on a sample … it is clear that we have lost these elections," Vučić told supporters in Belgrade, putting the Students' List at 135–140 seats and his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) at about 105. A representative sample by the pollsters CeSID and Ipsos gave the students 138 seats and the SNS 104, with the rest going to ethnic-minority parties. Partial results reported by Le Monde suggest no other established party passed the 3% threshold, so the Socialist Party founded by Slobodan Milošević may leave parliament for the first time in 36 years. The Republic Electoral Commission put turnout at 64.89% at 18:00, two hours before polls closed; CeSID and Ipsos estimated 67.6% by 19:00, the highest since 1992. Final official results are still pending. Vučić blamed independent media, unnamed European countries and the "US deep state" for the loss, without giving evidence. The vote follows almost two years of protests that began after a station canopy collapsed in Novi Sad in November 2024, killing 16 people. Vučić resigned as president last month to run for prime minister, and the SNS has governed since 2012.
story.why: it ends more than a decade of SNS rule, and a government formed by the protest movement could change Serbia's course on EU accession and its ties with Russia.

story.headline: Machado returns to Venezuela from exile
story.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela on Sunday 25 October after almost a year in exile, and tens of thousands of supporters lined the roads to Caracas.
story.display_body: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela on Sunday 25 October after almost a year in exile, and tens of thousands of supporters lined the roads to Caracas. She reappeared at a church in Barquisimeto, about 350 km west of the capital, and her convoy took eight hours to reach Caracas through the crowds. How she got back into the country is not clear. Machado left in December 2025 to collect the Nobel Peace Prize, a few weeks before US forces seized President Nicolás Maduro in January. According to the Guardian and DW, the Trump administration has since backed interim President Delcy Rodríguez, a former Maduro deputy, rather than Machado, and reportedly opposed her return; she says she made several failed attempts to come home.
story.why: her return puts the main opposition leader back inside the country, against the interim government that Washington has chosen to work with.

story.headline: Zelensky confirms November talks with Russia
story.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed on Sunday 25 October that Russian and Ukrainian officials will meet in November under US mediation, after Moscow announced on Friday 23 October that talks would be held in Abu Dhabi.
story.display_body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed on Sunday 25 October that Russian and Ukrainian officials will meet in November under US mediation, after Moscow announced on Friday 23 October that talks would be held in Abu Dhabi. Peace talks have been stalled since early this year. In a national television interview, Zelensky said Ukraine was "ready to discuss", but that territory could only be negotiated by the two leaders, with other issues left to technical groups. The Kremlin has repeatedly refused a Zelensky–Putin meeting before a final peace deal. He again rejected Russian demands on Ukraine's army size, alliances and Western security guarantees, calling them "not negotiable", and repeated his call for a ceasefire on strikes against energy infrastructure ahead of winter. Russia rejects any pause in fighting before a deal.
story.why: it would be the first direct Russia–Ukraine round in months, but both sides' core positions are unchanged.

story.headline: Bulgaria heads to tight presidential runoff
story.summary: Bulgaria's presidential election goes to a runoff on Sunday 1 November after incumbent Iliana Iotova led the first round on Sunday 25 October with only 34.7%, just ahead of pro-European challenger Andrei Gyurov on 32%.
story.display_body: Bulgaria's presidential election goes to a runoff on Sunday 1 November after incumbent Iliana Iotova led the first round on Sunday 25 October with only 34.7%, just ahead of pro-European challenger Andrei Gyurov on 32%. The provisional figures cover 98.9% of polling records. Polls had given Iotova, who favours dialogue with Russia, between 40% and 47%. Turnout was 22% of 6.6 million registered voters, the lowest since the first post-communist presidential election in 1992. Iotova is backed by Prime Minister Rumen Radev, who resigned the presidency to campaign before his party won an absolute majority in April's parliamentary election.

story.headline: Migros plans to merge its ten cooperatives
story.summary: Migros announced on Monday 26 October that it plans to merge its ten regional cooperatives into a single group cooperative, the biggest change to its structure since founder Gottlieb Duttweiler chose a decentralised model in the 1940s.
story.display_body: Migros announced on Monday 26 October that it plans to merge its ten regional cooperatives into a single group cooperative, the biggest change to its structure since founder Gottlieb Duttweiler chose a decentralised model in the 1940s. The boards of all ten cooperatives and of the Federation of Migros Cooperatives approved the plan unanimously. The 2.3 million cooperative members will vote on it in mid-2027, and it needs a two-thirds majority in each of the ten regions. The supermarket business would be run nationally, and the regional leadership structures would be replaced by six regional councils, including one for French-speaking Switzerland and one for Ticino. Migros gave no figures for savings or job losses. The SonntagsZeitung reported that about 3,000 jobs could go and that the savings could reach CHF 300–400 million a year. Migros says the changes mainly affect administration and management, not shop staff, and promises no restructuring-related layoffs in the regional cooperatives until at least mid-2028. Group chief Mario Irminger and supermarket head Peter Diethelm will step down at the time of the members' vote.
story.why: Switzerland's largest retailer, with about 100,000 staff, is reorganising after selling Hotelplan, Melectronics and other businesses since 2024, and the job cuts would fall in regional head offices across the country, including Vaud.

story.headline: Parmelin to sign upgraded China trade deal
story.summary: The federal economics department announced on Monday 26 October that President Guy Parmelin will meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in China on Friday 30 October and sign the upgraded Switzerland–China free-trade agreement.
story.display_body: The federal economics department announced on Monday 26 October that President Guy Parmelin will meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in China on Friday 30 October and sign the upgraded Switzerland–China free-trade agreement. Negotiations to update the 2014 agreement, which was China's first with a country in continental Europe, ended in August. The amending protocol improves access to the Chinese market for Swiss goods and investment, and according to the federal economics department it strengthens the agreement's environmental and labour rules. Parmelin will also meet the ministers of commerce, social affairs, education and science, and open the 10th Sino-Swiss Economic Forum; the visit runs until Saturday 31 October. China is Switzerland's third-largest trading partner after the EU and the US. The communiqué does not say whether human rights are on the agenda; a separate Swiss–China human-rights dialogue was held on 20 October.
story.why: the upgrade improves Swiss exporters' access to their third-largest market, while the government's own communiqué leaves the human-rights side of the relationship out of the visit programme.

story.headline: Swiss real wages flat in 2026
story.summary: The Federal Statistical Office reported on Monday 26 October that wages under Switzerland's main collective labour agreements rose by an average of 0.5% in 2026, and minimum wages by 0.8%, so real wages are not expected to rise this year.
story.display_body: The Federal Statistical Office reported on Monday 26 October that wages under Switzerland's main collective labour agreements rose by an average of 0.5% in 2026, and minimum wages by 0.8%, so real wages are not expected to rise this year. The increase compares with 1.2% in 2025 and 2.1% in 2024. Forecast inflation for 2026 is 0.6%, which cancels out the nominal gain. Rises ranged from 1.2% in transport and storage to 0.3% in manufacturing and 0.2% in construction. Just under 700,000 people are covered by the agreements on actual wages, and about 1.85 million by agreements on minimum wages.
story.why: after two years of real gains, workers on collective agreements are back to flat purchasing power, and industry and construction workers lose ground.

story.headline: Swiss Ebola patient flown home from Nigeria
story.summary: A Swiss woman infected with Ebola in Nigeria is being flown to Switzerland for treatment, together with her husband, according to Nigeria's health minister, Muhammad Ali Pate.
story.display_body: A Swiss woman infected with Ebola in Nigeria is being flown to Switzerland for treatment, together with her husband, according to Nigeria's health minister, Muhammad Ali Pate. The woman, who is married to a staff member at the Swiss embassy in Abuja, was diagnosed on 20 October. Pate said her condition had improved markedly: she was stable and conscious, and her lab values were close to normal. He added that she may still be infectious, so strict protective measures apply. Her husband has no symptoms. The Federal Office of Public Health did not confirm the transfer at first, and the foreign ministry said it would give details later on Monday. Switzerland has two reference hospitals for diseases like Ebola, the University Hospitals of Zurich and Geneva.
